channel.title: Daily Gaming & Tech Brief
channel.description: Daily gaming, tech, Steam, Linux, free games, Xodus, and PC DRM news.

item.title: Daily Gaming & Tech Brief — September 17, 2026
item.description:
1. GAME NEWS

Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds starts its Year Two content push

Sega has outlined more content for Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds as it moves into its second year. The update includes free guest characters and additional post-launch content, keeping the game's live-service-style roadmap active after its initial launch period.

Shinji Mikami receives Hall of Fame recognition

Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami is being recognized with a Hall of Fame induction, highlighting his long-running influence on survival horror and action-game design. His career spans major work at Capcom and later Tango Gameworks, including Resident Evil 4 and The Evil Within.

Dragon's Dogma II: Dark Arisen gets a new trailer

Capcom has shown new material for Dragon's Dogma II: Dark Arisen, continuing promotion around the expanded version of the RPG. The project is part of the current wave of major Japanese publisher announcements and updates surrounding the series.

2. TECH NEWS

Valve develops new SteamOS compatibility layers for Steam Frame

Valve is working on FEX and Lepton components for Steam Frame, with the technology aimed at running software across the device's Linux-based environment. The work includes Android APK support and reflects Valve's broader effort to make SteamOS hardware compatible with software outside the traditional x86 PC model.

Linux gaming compatibility work continues to expand

Current Linux gaming development continues to focus on compatibility layers, game-specific fixes and improving support for software distributed through Steam. Recent tracking also shows ongoing changes to Linux depots and compatibility-related packaging as developers adapt games for the platform.

3. STEAM SALE / EVENT

Steam Programming Fest — September 17–20

Steam's Programming Fest is active from September 17 through September 20, focusing on games built around programming and related mechanics. It is part of Steam's September event schedule, alongside the Party-Based RPG Fest running through September 21.

4. XODUS

Progress: active development toward game execution

Current Xodus development remains focused on getting Windows games running through its compatibility stack. Recent project activity continues around implementation, packaging and dependency work, but there is no defensible public percentage for overall game-execution progress, so no numeric progress bar is included.

5. FREE GAMES

Epic Games Store

Astral Ascent and Luftrausers are the current Epic Games Store free-to-keep games around September 17. The next giveaway window is scheduled to bring Mindcop and Shogun Showdown from September 17 through September 24.

6. LINUX APPS

FEX

An open-source x86/x86-64 userspace emulator that is increasingly relevant to Linux gaming and ARM-based hardware, including Valve's Steam Frame work.

Lepton

Valve's compatibility work for Steam Frame includes Lepton as part of the software stack intended to broaden what applications can run on the device.

Prism Launcher

An open-source Minecraft launcher for Linux with strong support for separate instances, mod loaders and per-instance configuration.

7. PIRACY SCENE

Denuvo vs. voices38 lawsuit filed

Denuvo's parent company has filed a lawsuit against the piracy group voices38, seeking damages and injunctive relief. Reporting says the complaint names 26 games and follows the group's recent activity involving Denuvo-protected releases.

Denuvo removals continue

Recent tracking reports Denuvo being removed from several games, including Code Vein II, Mega Man Star Force Legacy Collection, Bravely Default Flying Fairy HD Remaster and Dragon's Dogma 2. These removals are changes to the games' DRM configuration rather than new cracks.

DRM circumvention activity remains unusually active

The current PC DRM scene continues to include conventional crack releases, updates and research into alternative approaches to protected games. Confirmed developments should be distinguished from community rumors, especially where a release or bypass has not been independently verified.
